correctness.rationale: For any non-singleton connected initial set, the first nonempty force from part V_i requires at most k initially white vertices outside V_i; after it, more than k whites remaining inside V_i cannot be forced. Connectivity supplies initially black vertices on both sides, yielding the two additional part-capacity bounds. The matching construction realizes both caps. The singleton case is exactly the universal-vertex case. Exhaustive direct simulation through order nine agrees in all 524 parameter cases.

value.rationale: This is a natural exact solution for the complete-multipartite family of a recently introduced hybrid forcing/domination invariant. It unifies several separately published boundary formulas and reduces the optimum to a transparent two-cap expression with a sharp universal-vertex exception. The theorem is analytic and family-wide, not a finite census or routine recomputation.
